title: Long FDX — Q4 FY2026 Beat Event; Bernstein $424 PT Implies 30% Upside
entry: Long $320–332 (FDX at $326.20 pre-earnings June 23; enter before 5 PM EDT close today to capture the after-hours report). Scale: 1/2 position on entry today; add 1/2 only if after-hours reaction is positive (FDX $330+) and the next-day open confirms above $328. Do NOT initiate after an initial drop of more than 5% in after-hours — the thesis depends on a clean earnings beat, not a catch-down. If the market opens below $315 on June 24 reaction, exit the entire position without adding.
stop_loss: $308 daily close (~5.7% below $327 midpoint) — implies FDX Q4 earnings missed on revenue or package volume guidance for FY2027 disappointed materially, OR management explicitly flagged freight pricing weakness and industrial demand deceleration that calls the post-ceasefire recovery thesis into question; at $308, the post-Bernstein upgrade story is broken regardless of any broader market recovery
targets: $342 — Bernstein's base re-rating target for a clean Q4 beat (revenue +4–6% YoY, Ground margin expansion, FY2027 guidance in-line); sell-side confirmation upgrades triggered; +4.6% from $327 midpoint; take 50% of position

$365 — extended re-rating: FY2027 guidance raised above consensus ($38.50B+ revenue), operating margin guidance implies structural e-commerce shift from B2C to B2B/industrial is sustainable into the macro recovery; +11.6%; take 30%

$420 — Bernstein's $424 PT realized: volume inflection in Ground and Express segments confirms that the Iran oil shock demand destruction has fully normalized; freight tonnage comps turn positive; FY2028 earnings power re-rated by Street to $35+ EPS; +28.4%; hold final 20% through the FY2027 Q1 setup
risk_reward: 1:5.0 to third target (from $327 mid; stop $308 = $19 risk; T3 $420 = $93 gain)
catalyst: FedEx Q4 FY2026 earnings report after market close June 23 (5 PM EDT). Bernstein analyst recently issued a $424 price target on FDX, representing approximately 30% upside from the $326 trading price — one of the most bullish Street calls on the stock. Consensus estimates for Q4 FY2026: revenue approximately $22.0–22.5B, EPS $5.50–6.00 (management guided for improvement). FDX has lagged the broader market recovery from the Iran oil shock and the post-FOMC rally; the stock trades at only ~15x forward EPS, a discount to both the S&P 500 and to historical FDX multiples of 18–22x. Macro tailwinds include: Brent oil at $77.90 (from highs above $95 during the conflict period) reduces fuel surcharge drag, the Iran general license issued by Treasury unlocks overland freight volume through trade corridors that were suspended, and the e-commerce volume cycle is in the early stages of its post-disruption recovery following the supply chain normalization. The same June 23–24 session that has NVDA Annual Meeting and MU earnings is thus also the FDX earnings window — three major catalyst events in a compressed 24-hour period create elevated volatility.
thesis:
FedEx enters Q4 FY2026 earnings from a structurally undervalued position relative to the oil-relief and macro-recovery thesis that has driven airlines and transports broadly higher since the Iran ceasefire. UAL has rallied on the same $77.90 Brent backdrop; FDX has not — the lag is the opportunity. The oil decline materially improves FDX's fuel cost line: aviation fuel and diesel represent approximately 11–13% of FDX revenue; a $20/barrel decline from the conflict peak translates into roughly $400–600M in annualized fuel cost relief (net of hedges and surcharges), with Q4 FY2026 the first quarter to fully capture the relief. This alone argues for operating leverage above what consensus models, before any volume improvement.

The Bernstein $424 price target, implying 30% upside, rests on a volume and pricing thesis that has a clear catalyst in the FY2027 guidance framework. The Street consensus for FDX Ground margin has been anchored to the post-pandemic period when B2C e-commerce pulled forward demand and then normalized violently. If FDX Q4 demonstrates that Ground margins have stabilized above 8% and that B2B/industrial freight (less price-sensitive, higher margin) is returning as the Iran-disrupted supply chains re-normalize, the multiple can expand from the current ~15x to the 18–20x range consistent with a logistics business that is cycling out of a one-time demand shock — not experiencing structural volume decline.

The macro regime headwind is the primary risk to sizing this at low conviction rather than medium. STEP ASIDE is the morning's regime verdict: all three gates (VIX, DXY, BTC) are simultaneously breached, meaning the macro backdrop does not support broad long exposure. FDX earnings is a company-specific event that can override the macro regime for a 2–5 day window — Q4 results are either a beat or a miss regardless of VIX — but the surrounding regime means any soft guidance will be punished more than in a HOLD or BUY regime. The 2% position size and $308 stop reflect the elevated regime-level risk; in a HOLD regime, this would be a 4–5% position.

The counter-party is the freight bear who argues: (1) FDX Ground volume growth has been structurally impaired by Amazon's buildout of its own logistics network (Amazon Logistics now handles >70% of its own last-mile delivery in the US); (2) the industrial freight recovery is slower than the consumer sentiment indicators suggest — PMI manufacturing has been contracting for three of the last four months; (3) FDX's $2.9B DRIVE cost-reduction program is running out of easy cuts, and the remaining efficiency targets require volume growth that hasn't materialized. These are durable structural concerns; they make this a 2–5 day event trade rather than a position trade, with the $308 stop enforcing discipline if the print disappoints.
bull_case: FDX Q4 beats revenue consensus by 3–4% ($22.8B+), Ground margins print at 9.1% (above expectations), and FY2027 guidance implies $24.5B+ Q1 with operating margin expanding. Fuel cost relief is explicitly quantified as $500M annualized tailwind. Bernstein reiterates $424 PT and two additional firms upgrade from Hold to Buy within one week. FDX surges 8–12% in after-hours, opens above $350 on June 24, and tests the $365 target within the week.
bear_case: FDX Q4 revenue in-line ($22.1B) but FY2027 Q1 guidance is soft ($21.5–22.0B) on continued B2C volume weakness and Amazon logistics displacement. Ground margin prints at 7.8% (below expectations). Management acknowledges that fuel cost relief has been partially offset by volume deleverage and wage inflation. Stock drops 6–9% in after-hours, opens below $308 on June 24, triggering the stop. Position exited at full loss.
invalidation: $308 daily close; OR FDX Q4 revenue misses consensus by more than 3% (sub-$21.5B); OR FY2027 operating margin guidance below 7.5% (structural margin compression confirmed); OR management explicitly cites Amazon logistics competition as causing sustained volume displacement (not cyclical but structural); OR after-hours FDX falls more than 5% on the initial print (entry thesis broken pre-market open June 24)
